display_name: OpenAI Moderation API (cloud-native, wrapped by LiteLLM)
install_tell: OpenAI-managed endpoint at https://api.openai.com/v1/moderations; bearer sk-* key in Authorization header. Models: omni-moderation-latest (default), text-moderation-latest.
misconfig_patterns: OPENAI_API_KEY in LiteLLM config used for BOTH chat completion and moderation; one leaked key burns both surfaces.

Operators routing moderation via a private OpenAI-compatible mirror (api_base override): when api_base is misconfigured to an attacker-controlled host, every moderated message is exfiltrated through the attacker; LiteLLM does no host-allowlisting on api_base.

result.flagged returns false on edge cases (multilingual jailbreaks, code-encoded prompts) where the model is unsure; operators sometimes treat 'not flagged' as 'safe' without realizing the moderation API is best-effort, not a security boundary.

active_probe.false_positive_check: All requests to api.openai.com look identical; identity = api_key, not endpoint. Not a discoverable surface from Shodan.

deployment_tells: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/moderations with Authorization: Bearer sk-...
LiteLLM-side: api_base default https://api.openai.com/v1 + Bearer token from OPENAI_API_KEY env
pivot_paths: Leaked OPENAI_API_KEY in public configs grants moderation quota AND chat completion quota; the moderation endpoint is the cheaper-to-prove use of a leaked key.
LiteLLM proxy that wraps OpenAI moderation inherits the LiteLLM CVE chain; same as Bedrock wrapper.

added_surface: api_base is operator-controlled and not allowlisted; misconfiguration redirects all moderated content to attacker host.
LiteLLM stores OPENAI_API_KEY in proxy .env; that file becomes the high-value target.

LiteLLM raises HTTPException(400) on flagged content but allows operators to set raise_exception=False (mask_response_content path); a misconfigured 'log only' mode lets harmful content through while operator dashboards report 'guardrail active'.
LiteLLM /guardrails/list discloses moderation guardrail presence to authenticated proxy users.
litellm_wrapper_delta.verdict: Mostly a transparent passthrough at the protocol layer (same POST /v1/moderations, same payload shape). The added surface is credential centralization and policy ambiguity (log-only vs enforce). The cloud API itself is unchanged.

disclosure_contact.channel_observed: security@openai.com / disclose.io (cloud vendor; not LiteLLM wrapper bugs)
